raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm 34, got seven mouths to feed at home, and my ten mu by the road is all we've got for the land work. My wife and I do most of it — the older one helps when he's not at school, and my cousin drives over with the combine when harvest comes. Been in these fields since I was a boy, so I mostly know what works.

---

**Wheat first (that's what goes in now, well, this past October really — but I'll tell you how I think about it each year):**

I plant wheat on all ten mu in early October, right after the corn comes off. I don't mess with fancy varieties — I use Jimai or whatever the agri-shop in town has that year, same as my neighbors. Seed is maybe 15 kg per mu, I broadcast a bit heavier if the seedbed looks rough.

For fertilizer I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) for about every two mu before planting — so about 25 kg per mu as base. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Wang does a bit more urea but I can't afford to every year. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll add a little more, otherwise I leave it.

Irrigation — I pump three times usually. Once before winter so the roots don't dry out, once at green-up with the topdress, once at booting when the heads are forming. The well is metered so each round costs me maybe 30 yuan a mu. If it rains good in spring I'll skip the green-up one to save money.

I spray once for weeds in spring, and if I see aphids around heading I spray again. Harvest is early June, I pay the combine man 60 yuan per mu.

Last year I got about 420 kg per mu. This year I'm hoping for similar — no reason to expect better or worse.

---

**Then maize, right after:**

The day the wheat comes off, the ground has to get turned and the maize has to go in. Can't wait — every day costs yield at the back end. I rotary till and plant the same day or next, hire the no-till planter if the ground is too dry.

Maize seed I always buy fresh — has to be hybrid, you can't save it. Something like Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop pushes, costs me about 60 yuan per mu for the seed. I'll do 4000-4500 plants per mu, maybe a little thicker than my father did.

Fertilizer: I put compound down with the planter, one bag per 2 mu same as wheat. Then when the corn is knee-high I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu. That's it — two rounds.

Irrigation — only if it doesn't rain. Usually the summer rains come and I don't pump at all, or maybe once at tasseling if July is dry. The maize is cheaper to grow than wheat because of the rain.

Spray once for corn borer at whorl stage, once for weeds early on. Harvest is end of September, hire the combine again. Last year I got 460 kg per mu.

---

**What worries me:**

Fertilizer prices keep going up. I used to buy three bags of urea, now the same money buys two. If it goes up again I'll have to cut the topdress, and then yield drops. Diesel for the pump also — but the well is there, I have to use it.

My budget for the whole year for both crops is around 9,000 yuan, maybe 9,500. That's tight. Our off-farm money from my brother-in-law's shop covers the rest of what we need at home.
